correctness.rationale: Each cyclic tour is anchored by its unique edge 00000, so this counts rotation classes without dividing out complementation or reversal. A palindromic six-factor is a-v-a with v a palindromic four-bit vertex. The incoming-to-outgoing bijection gives both a=0 and a=1 palindromes or neither. At a constant vertex the direct bijection would map its unique loop to itself, impossible in a tour of 32 distinct edges. The two remaining centers, 0110 and 1001, give the claimed pairs; they are nonadjacent and their forced paths can be suppressed independently. Each shortcut retains its edge identity. The root loop remains first; for a degree-two balanced graph with that anchor the last exits at nonroot vertices form an in-tree and uniquely determine the edge orders, so the directed Laplacian cofactors count the required tours. Separate complete DFS replay anchored at 00000 visited 92636 calls and reconstructed and scanned all 2048 cycles, obtaining joint cells 768,512,512,256, in the order neither, first only, second only, both, with no other palindrome. The anchored scan counts distinct circular factors. The table gives E[P]=3/2, E[P^2]=4, variance 7/4 and covariance 1/8-(3/8)^2=-1/64. The frozen script was inspected, not executed. Independent replay and output: /workspace/branches/32969e6a-348e-41e3-b85d-7a4e5362dc50/palindrome_enum.py and palindrome_enum_result.json in the same directory. This is a complete finite result for order five only.

value.rationale: The joint table is naturally motivated: order five permits simultaneous presence of two nonconstant centers, whereas at order four the two nonconstant palindromic centers cannot both pair directly without isolating the alternating two-edge orbit. But the precise table and negative covariance are already available. Re-evaluating four small cofactors using standard BEST and Matrix–Tree is useful corroboration, not an independently valuable new finding under the frozen scope. No distinct surviving research claim is established.
